chapterBreakdown.gentle:
Once objective ignorance is visible, another difficult zone comes into focus. The chapter turns to the valley of the normal.

That move matters because ordinary-looking cases are not automatically easy. Middle or borderline judgments can still resist crisp agreement, and that makes them fertile ground for noise.

This is where the distinction matters. Extreme cases may force clearer answers, but the ordinary middle can leave more room for divergence. The chapter uses that middle zone to show how normal-range ambiguity can keep variation alive.

The chapter keeps one useful limit in place. It is not claiming that only middle cases matter, and it is not abandoning structure. The point is narrower and more practical. Apparently normal cases can still be hard to classify cleanly.

That is what earns the next move. Once the ordinary middle has been shown to generate disagreement, the book can ask how noise happens more generally.
chapterBreakdown.direct:
The chapter turns from objective ignorance to the valley of the normal. It argues that normal-range cases can still generate disagreement because they resist clean classification.

That matters because noise analysis would stay too narrow if only dramatic extremes were treated as difficult. The ordinary middle can also invite divergence when a case is neither clearly one thing nor another.

This is the distinction the chapter has to hold. The ordinary appearance of a case does not make it simple, and the middle range can remain unstable even when the system is disciplined.

The limit stays visible. The chapter is not saying only ordinary cases matter, and it is not turning away from judgment structure. It is claiming something narrower: normal-looking borderline cases can still keep disagreement alive.

That prepares the next step. Once the valley of the normal is visible, the book can turn to the broader mechanism question of how noise gets generated.
chapterBreakdown.competitive:
The chapter goes from blindness to ordinary-looking ground that still makes the room split. It asks what happens when the middle of the scale starts wobbling.

That matters because the book wants to kill the lazy comfort that only obvious edge cases are hard. The plain-looking middle can also resist a clean call, and that keeps the wobble alive.

This is where the chapter gets sharper. The middle zone is not mystical, and it is not trivial. It is simply a place where classification gets harder because the case does not shout its answer.

The discipline stays narrow on purpose. No one is saying the middle is the only battleground, and no one is dropping the value of structure. The point is that ordinary-looking terrain can still divide the room.

That is what earns the next step. Once the middle band starts wobbling, the next question is what keeps producing wobble in the first place.

chapterBreakdown.gentle:
Once objective ignorance is visible, another difficult zone comes into focus. The chapter turns to the valley of the normal.

That move matters because ordinary-looking cases are not automatically easy. Middle or borderline judgments can still resist crisp agreement, and that makes them fertile ground for noise.

Hard depth sharpens the distinction. The ordinary middle is not mysterious because it hides secret magic. It is difficult because it often fails to force a clean classification, leaving more room for divergence across judges.

The chapter keeps one useful limit in place. It is not claiming that only middle cases matter, and it is not abandoning structure. The point is to show that apparently normal terrain can still produce hard disagreement.

This is what changes after the chapter on objective ignorance. The question is no longer only what the system cannot know, but also why ordinary-looking cases remain unstable even when they are not extreme.

That is what makes the next move feel earned. Once the ordinary middle has been shown to wobble, the book can ask how noise gets produced more generally.
chapterBreakdown.direct:
The chapter turns from objective ignorance to the valley of the normal. It argues that normal-range cases can still generate disagreement because they resist clean classification.

That matters because noise analysis would stay too shallow if only edge cases were treated as difficult. Middle cases can also remain unstable, and the room for divergence often lives in that ordinary-looking zone.

This is the harder distinction it wants to hold. The ordinary middle is a source of disagreement not because it is mystical, but because it often leaves classification underdetermined enough for judges to part ways.

The limit remains essential. The chapter adds the middle zone to the map of noise without claiming it replaces every other source of variation or difficulty.

That is what sets up the next move. Once the valley of the normal has shown how variation can live in ordinary cases, the book can turn to the broader question of how noise happens.

That matters because the book wants to strip away the lazy comfort that only dramatic edge cases are hard. Plain-looking terrain can also refuse a clean call, and the room can start splitting right there.

This is where the chapter gets exact. The middle zone is not mystical and it is not boring. It is dangerous because it gives the room just enough ambiguity to lean in different directions.

The discipline stays narrow on purpose. No one is worshipping the middle band, and no one is pretending structure stops mattering there. The chapter is naming one more place where wobble survives.
